turns.speaker: user
turns.text: My wife uses a wheelchair and we want to visit Amsterdam. Is that realistic?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Definitely realistic, with some planning. The canals and cobbles can be tricky, but trams and many museums are accessible.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: What about hotels? Old buildings with steep stairs worry me.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Book a newer hotel and call them directly to confirm a step free entrance, a lift and an accessible bathroom. Photos help too.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Good idea. And getting from the airport?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: The train from the airport to the central station has step free access, and staff can help with a ramp if you book assistance.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: She'd love a canal boat. Can she

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: actually get on one of those?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Some operators have wheelchair accessible boats. Look for them specifically and book ahead, they're limited.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Then I'd book it first. Everything else can fit around it.
